findings.anchor: query = f"SELECT id, status, total FROM orders WHERE customer_id = '{owner_id}'"
findings.body: The query string is constructed using f-string interpolation with an unsanitized owner_id parameter. This creates a SQL injection vulnerability where a malicious owner_id value can alter the query logic or exfiltrate data. Use parameterized queries instead.
findings.failure_scenario: An attacker passes owner_id="' OR '1'='1" which modifies the WHERE clause to return all orders regardless of customer, or passes owner_id="'; DROP TABLE orders; --" to execute arbitrary SQL.
findings.suggestion:
query = "SELECT id, status, total FROM orders WHERE customer_id = %s"
cursor.execute(query, (owner_id,))
findings.title: SQL injection vulnerability in load_order_rows

findings.anchor: def register_shipment_events(event_type: str, events: list[str] = []) -> dict[str, list[str]]:
findings.body: The function uses a mutable list as a default argument (events: list[str] = []). This is a Python anti-pattern: the same list object is reused across all function calls, causing unexpected state sharing between invocations. Each call will append to the same list, leading to accumulated events from previous calls.
findings.failure_scenario: First call: register_shipment_events('ship') returns {'ship': ['ship']}. Second call: register_shipment_events('deliver') returns {'deliver': ['ship', 'deliver']} instead of {'deliver': ['deliver']}, because the default list persists.
findings.title: Mutable default argument in register_shipment_events

findings.anchor: def flag_large_backorder_totals(rows: list[dict[str, object]], threshold: float) -> list[dict[str, object]]:
findings.body: The function accepts a threshold parameter but does not use it; instead, it hardcodes the value 5000 in the comparison. This is misleading: callers expect the threshold argument to control the filtering logic, but it is ignored. Either use the parameter or remove it from the signature.
findings.failure_scenario: A caller passes threshold=10000 expecting rows with total > 10000 to be flagged, but the function returns only rows with total > 5000, silently ignoring the caller's intent.
findings.title: Unused threshold parameter in flag_large_backorder_totals
